title: LLM-Assisted Reranking to Operationalize Nuanced Objectives in Recommender Systems
abstract: arXiv:2606.02883v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Recommender systems shape what information we see, raising concerns about filter bubbles, radicalization, polarization, and social inequality. Large language models (LLMs) enable more powerful personalization that may intensify these dynamics, yet most recommenders are tuned for engagement or narrow accuracy metrics, with little attention to broader social effects. We investigate whether LLM-assisted reranking, while improving personalization, inadvertently amplifies exposure to ideologically congenial, extreme, or conspiratorial political content, a risk theorized but not yet empirically characterized. Using real YouTube trajectories, we rerank the platform's sidebar candidates by zero-shot prompting across three models, alongside an embedding baseline, and evaluate relevance, ideological alignment and diversity, and exposure to conspiratorial or extremist content. translated_title: 基于大语言模型辅助的重排序：在推荐系统中实现细致目标
translated_abstract: 推荐系统塑造了我们能看到的信息，引发了人们对信息茧房、激进化、极化和社会不平等的担忧。大语言模型（LLM）能够实现更强大的个性化，但这可能加剧上述动态，然而大多数推荐系统都只为参与度或狭窄的准确性指标进行调优，很少关注更广泛的社会影响。我们研究了大语言模型辅助的重排序在提升个性化的同时，是否会无意中放大用户接触意识形态上契合的、极端的或阴谋论式政治内容的风险——这一风险此前仅在理论上被提出，尚未得到实证刻画。利用真实的YouTube浏览轨迹，我们通过零样本提示对三个大语言模型（并与嵌入基线对比）对平台侧边栏候选内容进行重排序，并评估相关性、意识形态一致性与多样性，以及接触阴谋论或极端主义内容的情况。我们发现（i）在纯个性化指令下，重……（摘要原文在此处截断）
tldr: 本文基于真实YouTube轨迹实证检验了大语言模型辅助的重排序在提升个性化推荐的同时，是否会放大用户接触意识形态同质化、极端或阴谋论政治内容的风险。
en_tdlr: This paper empirically examines, using real YouTube trajectories, whether LLM-assisted reranking improves personalization while inadvertently amplifying exposure to ideologically homogeneous, extreme, or conspiratorial political content.
